## p191 A1, p191 A2 — p191 A — Boots and clothing for Oderberg

<a id="edition-cases-military-p191-a-p191-a--boots-and-clothing-for-oderberg"></a>



**Status: body recovered with a conditional five-coordinate group move;
unit/quantity symbols and one connective remain unresolved.** The two
parts fix **196 of 200 plaintext positions** after four explicit
known-coordinate substitutions and twelve printed-dash fills. Their
lengths remain 214 and 186 coordinates, and the published key is unchanged.

The message asks a deputy corps command at Breslau to make boots and
heavy clothing available initially for Oderberg, on call and with advance
notice. A wire/radio reply is requested. The repaired signature is
`A.O.K.11`. The exact corps symbol and number of pairs of boots are not
supplied from historical plausibility.

The literal spellings `SELLV` and `BEKLEIDNG` remain in these strings.
Expanding them in prose adds no characters to the ciphertext edition.
Punctuation, word division and abbreviation expansion are editorial.

The three unresolved part-1 symbols occupy distinct cells `GD`, `FV`
and `XX`, each with domain `{2,3,4,7,8,9,Q,Y}`. Their assignments must
be different. The part-2 connective keeps the full domain
`{0,2,3,4,7,8,9,O,Q,U,W,Y}`. Readable `O`/`U` possibilities do not
reduce that domain or select *oder* versus *und*.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p191-a-compatibility-with-the-shared-headquarters-reading"></a>

#### Compatibility with the shared headquarters reading

The later [XX=Q headquarters interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-intendants-address)
has an adverse consequence here: the unaltered quantity becomes **`?0Q0`**.
It cannot be read as a decimal count without a source correction. Under
both that Q assignment and the independent [FX=Y courier-name interpretation](192.md#edition-cases-caucasus-tiflis-appointment-the-separate-historical-name-inference),
the unique one-coordinate repair making this character numerical is
**X→D at source position 102**, giving **`?000`**. These indices are zero-based.
The possible quantities are 3000, 4000, 7000, 8000 or 9000; none is selected.
Without the Y assumption, other one-coordinate numerical repairs survive.

This is a priced compatibility proposal, not an additional recovered count.
The primary edition and its four unresolved positions above remain the
baseline. [Exact neighbouring-coordinate check](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/compatibility_certificate.json).

<a id="edition-cases-military-p191-a-the-displaced-group"></a>

### The displaced group

The untouched second part decrypts to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UFTERAORVELDUHGMFJST?R?EPPEKLE?DN6AUFA?R?IBERE?T5KELLE??A?RAHT??CNUNKA?T?URTER?E?ENXXA?OEJX1?
```

</details>

Move printed group **12**, `AXFVA`, immediately before printed group
**8**, preserving all coordinate values and every other group order:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional move of printed group 12 immediately before group 8:**

```text
UNTERVORMELDUNGMITST?R?ERBEKLE?DNGAUFA?RUFBERE?TSTELLE??XDRAHT??XFUNKA?TWORTER?ETENXXA?O5KX1?
```

</details>

Only two further observed-coordinate changes are needed in this part,
both `F → V` at original coordinates 127 and 130, plus eleven dash
fills. One source erasure remains at the connective.

The geometry check masks the entire footer and uses 77 ordinary-word
positions, with no names, unit numbers or quantities. Across the identity
and **all one-complete-group moves** among 37 complete groups—1,333
operations, 1,297 distinct streams—the displayed move is the sole
zero-disagreement candidate. The untouched source has nineteen
ordinary-word coordinate disagreements. A fresh control with the same
length, twelve erased positions and group displacement likewise recovers
its true order as the unique zero-disagreement candidate.

The word mask was developed after inspecting the damaged source, so
this is a conditional consistency check, not a blind language experiment
or a proof that no other error mechanism is possible. The certificate
retains all minimizing operations, not a chosen tie.

### Source and exact accounting

[Source crop](../../experiments/boots_request/sources/childs_p191_A.png):
Childs printed p191 / PDF p194. The heading gives **14 November 1918**.
The header is `LP v ZÖN (06.16 p.m., November ?); 2301 (11/14) 2 TLE`;
the intercept-day question mark is preserved.

| Measure | Part 1 | Part 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Coordinate slots / printed erasures | 214 / 1 | 186 / 12 |
| Untouched raw fixed positions | 102/107 | 76/93 |
| Proposed fixed positions | 104/107 | 92/93 |
| Five-coordinate group moves | 0 | 1 |
| Observed-coordinate substitutions | 2 | 2 |
| Printed-dash fills | 1 | 11 |
| Insertions / deletions | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Part 1 repairs `D?INGENDER` and `S1IEFEL` with counted substitutions,
and fills its dash for the separator following the quantity. Part 2
repairs the adjective and footer separator after the group move. All
edits are expressed in original printed coordinates. Every value in the
remaining connective domain has a joint, injective square witness for
both messages; arbitrary witness digits are not proposed readings.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p191-a-optional-breslau-unit-emendation"></a>

### Optional Breslau unit emendation

A [separate primary-source supplement](../../experiments/boots_request/breslau_context/README.md)
records a visually inspected VI Army Corps decree dated Breslau, 6 July 1917,
published in the *Waldenburger Wochenblatt*, 18 July 1917. A closer witness
is the decree dated **Breslau, 11 November 1918**, printed in *Der Gebirgsbote*
on **13 November 1918**, which names the same deputy command of **VI Army
Corps** alongside the soldiers' council. [Original decree crop](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/breslau_vi_corps_nov11.png)
· [source and verification](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#a-separate-breslau-unit-interpretation).
This supports the recipient identification within the week of the telegram.
The optional reading still requires the already priced source change D→G at coordinate 162,
reading the existing GG=6 cell and giving 197/200 fixed positions. This is not
a fill of the received GD cell, whose domain excludes 6. The primary 196/200
edition above, the quantity and all connective alternatives remain unchanged.
